newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-DORANS PRIDE MAY WAIT FOR GOLD CUP BID.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DORANS PRIDE MAY WAIT FOR GOLD CUP BID.

text.p: Trainer Michael Hourigan hinted on Saturday that Ireland's top novice chaser Dorans Pride might not go for the Cheltenham Gold Cup in 1997.
"It's a bit soon to be thinking about the Gold Cup. Maybe we'll wait for another year," Hourigan said after his stable-star had won a minor race at Leopardstown.
"We might go for one of the other top chases instead," he added.
Despite the trainer's remarks, Dublin bookmakers quoted Dorans Pride at 12-1 for the 1997 Gold Cup after Saturday's easy victory.
He started the 5-1 on-favourite and led his three rivals for all of the three miles (4.8-km) trip to win by a distance (over 30 lengths).
"He couldn't have done it better than he did. He jumped well when he quickened and showed he's well able to look after himself," Hourigan said.
Regular partner Shane Broderick was back on board after missing the horse's previous win because of suspension. Dorans Pride has now won 15 of his 23 starts and been runner-up six times.
There was a tragic end to the Ericsson Chase when the winner, Johnny Setaside, suffered a heart attack on his way back to the winner's enclosure and died.
Johnny Setaside, ridden by Richard Dunwoody, had edged out Arthur Moore's King of the Gales by three lengths at the end of the three miles (4.8-km) trip.
Imperial Call, the Cheltenham Gold Cup winner, missed the race after failing to recover from an injury sustained in a fall at Punchestown last time out.
Trainer Fergie Sutherland says Imperial Call is likely to make a re-appearance in the Hennessy Gold Cup at Leopardstown on February 2, a race he won in style last season.
